items.stem: Converting a model's weights from FP32 to INT8 most directly achieves which outcome?

options.text: About a 4x reduction in weight memory footprint
options.rationale: Correct: INT8 uses 8 bits vs 32, roughly quartering weight storage.

options.text: A guaranteed increase in model accuracy
options.rationale: Quantisation typically reduces or holds accuracy; it does not raise it.

options.text: Elimination of the need for calibration data
options.rationale: Static PTQ still needs calibration data to set scales.

items.explanation: Correct: INT8 uses 8 bits vs 32, roughly quartering weight storage.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about quantisation-aware training (QAT) are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: QAT simulates quantisation during training so the model adapts to it
options.rationale: Correct: QAT inserts fake-quant ops so weights learn to tolerate low precision.

options.text: QAT generally recovers more accuracy than post-training quantisation at very low precision
options.rationale: Correct: by training under quantisation, QAT usually beats PTQ at aggressive bit-widths.

options.text: QAT requires no access to training data or pipeline
options.rationale: QAT needs the training loop and data; PTQ is the data-light option.

options.text: QAT is always cheaper than PTQ
options.rationale: QAT adds training cost, so it is more expensive, not cheaper.

items.explanation: Correct: QAT inserts fake-quant ops so weights learn to tolerate low precision.

items.stem: Unstructured magnitude pruning yields a sparse model but no speed-up on the target device. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: The hardware and runtime do not exploit unstructured sparsity
options.rationale: Correct: without sparse kernel support, zeros are still computed, so no speed-up.

options.text: Pruning never reduces the number of parameters
options.rationale: Pruning does zero out parameters; the issue is hardware exploitation.

options.text: The model was quantised instead of pruned
options.rationale: The scenario states pruning was applied.
Sparsity can speed inference where supported; here support is absent.

items.explanation: Correct: without sparse kernel support, zeros are still computed, so no speed-up.
